films.title: Robot Digs a Ditch, Gardener Shows a Swale
films.description: A robot digs a straight ditch down the hill, and the next rain races through it, away from every thirsty plant. An older gardener traces a level line across the slope instead. Together they dig a shallow swale on contour, with a berm on the downhill side. When rain comes, the swale fills, pauses, and slowly soaks in, feeding young fruit trees. A low spillway lets the extra spill over.

films.title: If Sickness Paid Nothing, Would We Still Be Sick?
films.description: In 2023, the world's top 100 arms makers took in $632 billion, rising on the back of wars (SIPRI). In 2024, America spent about $15,000 a person on health care, more than any other rich country, yet Americans live shorter lives than people in peer countries (Peterson-KFF, OECD data). When danger and illness pay, incentives point the wrong way. What if robots made safety, food and care a public good? Not a promise. A better question.

films.title: A Robot Piled Every Seed in One Spot
films.description: A robot rakes every acorn into one big pile under the old oak, so they'll be safe. But the sprouts come up crowded and pale in the shade. A girl points to a jay burying acorns far away, and forgetting a few. Seeds carried off by birds and animals have better odds, so the robot scatters seed across the hill. Years later, the hill is a young forest.

films.title: Robot Learns to Mulch, Kids Pick Ripe Tomatoes
films.description: A robot keeps watering tomato plants in cracked, sun-baked soil, and they keep wilting. An older gardener shows it a better way: a thick blanket of straw mulch. Shaded soil holds water longer and stays cooler, and the straw slowly feeds the soil life. Weeks later, two kids pick ripe tomatoes.

films.title: Robots Plant the Food Forest, Grandma Picks Free Fruit
films.description: Robots turn a bare slope into a food forest: canopy trees, fruiting shrubs, strawberries as ground cover, swales soaking up the rain. Years later, a grandmother walks up the hill and fills her basket. Plant for people you'll never meet.

films.title: Your Job Was Never the Point
films.description: Work is not your purpose in life. The people who thrive own things: land, machines, a say in the rules. What if we owned them together? Community land, shared robots, local power, food forests, rules written in the open.

films.description: A robot goes to pull the comfrey and an elder gardener stops it: gardeners chop its leaves to feed the soil. Don't fight the land; work with it.

films.title: If Superintelligence Studied a Forest First
films.description: Imagine teaching superintelligence its first lesson in a forest, not a data center: nothing is wasted, and the strongest system is the most connected. Abundance that is composted, cycled and shared.

films.description: What would you do with a Tuesday that is yours? Fish with your kid, finally paint, help a neighbour, sit quietly. A short film about the time robotics and AI could give back.

films.title: What if nobody ever had to go without?
films.description: Food, a home, medicine, clean water: every one of them comes down to work, energy and knowing how. A short film about what could change if superintelligence brought the knowing how, robotics the work, and clean energy powered both.
